entries.title: Pharmacognosy
entries.shortAnswer: Medicines from plants, microbes and other natural sources.
entries.deeper: Pharmacognosy is the study of drugs and drug leads that come from natural sources: plants, fungi, bacteria, marine organisms and animals. It covers how these materials are identified, collected, standardised and analysed, and how their active constituents are isolated and characterised.

entries.title: Pharmaceutics
entries.shortAnswer: Turning a drug into a safe, stable, usable medicine.
entries.deeper: Pharmaceutics is the science of designing, preparing and evaluating dosage forms such as tablets, capsules, solutions, suspensions, creams and injections. It links the physical and chemical properties of a drug to how it is formulated, manufactured and used.

references.source: Standard pharmaceutics or dosage form design textbook (edition per your course)

entries.title: Pharmacology
entries.shortAnswer: How drugs act on the body, and how the body handles them.
entries.deeper: Pharmacology studies how drugs interact with biological systems. Pharmacodynamics describes what a drug does to the body, such as receptor binding and the resulting effect. Pharmacokinetics describes what the body does to a drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion.

references.source: Standard medical pharmacology textbook (edition per your course)

entries.title: Medicinal Chemistry
entries.shortAnswer: Designing and refining molecules that make good drugs.
entries.deeper: Medicinal chemistry applies organic and physical chemistry to design, synthesise and optimise drug molecules. It studies structure-activity relationships: how changing a molecule's structure changes its potency, selectivity, metabolism and safety.

references.source: Standard medicinal chemistry textbook (edition per your course)
references.purpose: Principles of structure-activity relationships and lead optimisation.
references.verify: Yes. Confirm title, author and edition before citing.

entries.title: Pharmaceutical Analysis
entries.shortAnswer: Measuring identity, purity and strength of medicines.
entries.deeper: Pharmaceutical analysis is the set of chemical and instrumental methods used to test the identity, purity, strength and quality of drug substances and drug products. Typical tools include titration, spectroscopy and chromatography.

references.source: ICH guideline on validation of analytical procedures (International Council for Harmonisation)

entries.title: Clinical Pharmacy
entries.shortAnswer: Optimising medicine use for individual patients.
entries.deeper: Clinical pharmacy focuses on the patient-facing use of medicines. It includes medication review, therapeutic monitoring, dose individualisation, interaction and adverse-effect assessment, and working with prescribers to reach safe, effective and appropriate therapy.

entries.title: Pharmacovigilance
entries.shortAnswer: Detecting and preventing harm from medicines after approval.
entries.deeper: Pharmacovigilance is the science and set of activities concerned with detecting, assessing, understanding and preventing adverse effects and other medicine-related problems. It relies on spontaneous reports, structured studies and signal detection.

entries.title: Pharmaceutical Microbiology
entries.shortAnswer: Keeping medicines and manufacturing environments safe from microbes.
entries.deeper: Pharmaceutical microbiology deals with microorganisms relevant to medicines: sterility, microbial limits, preservative effectiveness, sterilisation methods, contamination control and antimicrobial agents themselves.

entries.title: Biopharmaceutics
entries.shortAnswer: How a dosage form's design shapes what reaches the body.
entries.deeper: Biopharmaceutics examines how the physical and chemical properties of a drug, its dosage form and its route of administration affect the rate and extent of drug absorption and therefore its effect. Dissolution, solubility, permeability and bioavailability are central ideas.

entries.title: Biostatistics
entries.shortAnswer: Turning data into trustworthy conclusions.
entries.deeper: Biostatistics applies statistical methods to biological and health data. In pharmacy it supports trial design, analysis of results, bioequivalence assessment, quality control charts and interpretation of safety data.

entries.title: Pharmaceutical Biotechnology
entries.shortAnswer: Medicines made by or from living systems.
entries.deeper: Pharmaceutical biotechnology uses living cells and biological processes to produce medicines such as therapeutic proteins, monoclonal antibodies, vaccines and other biologics, and develops the methods to purify, characterise and formulate them.

entries.title: Nanotechnology
entries.shortAnswer: Engineering drug carriers at the scale of billionths of a metre.
entries.deeper: Nanotechnology in pharmacy involves designing carriers and materials at the nanometre scale, such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles and lipid nanoparticles, to change how a drug is dissolved, protected, distributed or released.

entries.title: Drug Discovery
entries.shortAnswer: Finding and validating new medicines.
entries.deeper: Drug discovery is the process of identifying a disease-relevant target, finding compounds that act on it, and optimising them into candidates suitable for testing. It integrates biology, chemistry, screening, computation and early safety assessment.

entries.title: Regulatory Science
entries.shortAnswer: The rules and evidence that decide what reaches patients.
entries.deeper: Regulatory science covers the frameworks, standards and assessment methods used to judge whether a medicine is of acceptable quality, safety and efficacy for authorisation and continued marketing, and to oversee manufacturing and distribution.

references.source: Your national medicines regulator's official website and legislation pages

entries.title: Industrial Pharmacy
entries.shortAnswer: Making medicines consistently at scale.
entries.deeper: Industrial pharmacy covers large-scale manufacture of medicines: scale-up from laboratory to production, unit operations such as mixing, granulation, compression and filling, process control, packaging, and quality systems.

entries.title: Community Pharmacy
entries.shortAnswer: The most accessible point of care for medicines advice.
entries.deeper: Community pharmacy is pharmacy practice in neighbourhood settings. It includes dispensing prescriptions, advising on non-prescription medicines and self-care, counselling patients, supporting adherence and, where permitted, providing services such as screening or vaccination.

entries.title: Public Health
entries.shortAnswer: Protecting and improving the health of populations.
entries.deeper: Public health focuses on preventing disease and promoting health at the population level. Pharmacists contribute through immunisation support, medicine access, antimicrobial stewardship, health education and supply chain quality.

entries.title: AI in Pharmacy
entries.shortAnswer: Machine learning and data tools applied across the pathway.
entries.deeper: AI in pharmacy refers to the use of machine learning and related computational methods to support tasks such as predicting molecular properties, screening compounds, analysing pharmacovigilance data and supporting clinical decision tools.

entries.title: Drug
entries.shortAnswer: A substance used to prevent, diagnose or treat disease, or to change a body function.
entries.deeper: In pharmacy a drug is studied from many angles at once: its structure, how it acts on the body, how it is formulated, how its quality is measured and how its safety is monitored. This site connects those angles rather than treating them separately.

entries.title: Mechanism
entries.shortAnswer: The specific way a drug produces its effect, usually by acting on a molecular target.
entries.deeper: Mechanism of action typically describes binding to a receptor, enzyme, transporter or ion channel and the downstream change that follows. Understanding mechanism helps predict effects, interactions and adverse reactions.

entries.deeper: Formulation combines the active substance with excipients and a manufacturing process to produce a tablet, capsule, liquid, cream, injection or other form. Choices here influence stability, release and patient acceptability.

entries.title: Microscope
entries.shortAnswer: Uses lenses to magnify small objects such as crude-drug tissues, powders, crystals and particles.
entries.deeper: An objective lens forms a magnified real image of the specimen, and an eyepiece magnifies that image again for the eye or a camera. Resolution depends on the wavelength of light and the numerical aperture of the objective, not on magnification alone.

entries.title: HPLC
entries.shortAnswer: High-performance liquid chromatography separates components of a mixture so each can be identified and measured.
entries.deeper: A pump pushes a liquid mobile phase at a controlled flow through a column packed with a stationary phase. Sample components interact differently with the two phases, so they leave the column at different times. A detector records each as a peak.

entries.title: UV-Vis spectrophotometer
entries.shortAnswer: Measures how much ultraviolet or visible light a solution absorbs, which can be related to concentration.
entries.deeper: A light source passes through a wavelength selector, then through the sample in a cuvette. A detector compares the light transmitted through the sample with a reference (blank). Absorbance is calculated from the ratio.

entries.title: Dissolution apparatus
entries.shortAnswer: Measures how quickly and how much of a drug dissolves from a dosage form under controlled conditions.
entries.deeper: A dosage form is placed in a vessel of dissolution medium held at a controlled temperature and agitated by a rotating basket or paddle at a set speed. Samples are withdrawn at time points and analysed.

entries.title: Tablet press
entries.shortAnswer: Compresses powder or granules into tablets of consistent shape, weight and hardness.
entries.deeper: Powder fills a die cavity from a feed system. Upper and lower punches move together and apply compression force, forming a tablet, which is then ejected. Rotary presses repeat this with many stations on a turret.

entries.title: Capsule filler
entries.shortAnswer: Fills empty capsule shells with a measured amount of powder, pellets or liquid and closes them.
entries.deeper: Empty capsule shells are separated into body and cap, the body is filled with a measured dose of the fill material, and the cap is rejoined. Dosing may use a tamping-pin dosator or a dosing disc, depending on the machine.

entries.title: Centrifuge
entries.shortAnswer: Spins samples at high speed so that denser components settle out of a mixture.
entries.deeper: A rotor spins tubes around an axis. The resulting centrifugal force is much larger than gravity, so denser particles move outward and settle to the bottom of the tube. RCF depends on rotor radius and rotation speed.
